tip: 'Få reda på' is a fixed phrase meaning to find out: 'fick reda på' = found out.
'Lite' means some or a little with uncountable nouns: 'lite mjölk' = some milk, with no plural.
'Hjälpa' uses 'med' for the task: 'hjälp din syster med läxorna' = help your sister with the homework.
'Vänta' takes 'på' for what you wait for: 'vänta på mig' = wait for me.
'Se ut att' means to seem or look like: 'ser ut att regna' = looks like it will rain.
On plural nouns the ending '-na' means the: 'tallrikar' (plates) becomes 'tallrikarna' = the plates.
In a definite noun phrase, front 'det', give the adjective '-a', and keep the noun's suffix: 'det svenska samhället' = the Swedish society.
'Det finns' is the set phrase for there is or there are: 'finns det andra fördelar' = there are other advantages.
Adding '-s' to the verb makes it passive: 'förbättrats' = had been improved.
'Klockan' plus a number gives clock time: 'klockan åtta' = at eight o'clock.
'För att' plus an infinitive expresses purpose, in order to: 'för att bli läkare' = to become a doctor.
In an 'att' clause 'inte' comes before the verb: 'att han inte hade rätt', not 'att han hade inte'.
'Man' is the generic subject for people in general: 'man säger' = they say or one says.
'Även om' means even if or even though: 'även om det var dyrt' = even though it was expensive.
In the definite, the adjective takes '-a' and the noun keeps its ending: 'det goda kaffet' (the good coffee).
The command form of 'ha' (to have) is just 'ha', used in wishes like 'ha en bra dag' (have a nice day).
With an 'ett' word the past participle adds '-t': 'riset är tillagat' (the rice is cooked).
In the phrasal verb 'värma upp' (heat up), the stress falls on 'upp': 'vi värmer upp maten'.
'Var snäll och...' (be kind and...) is a polite way to make requests in Swedish.
Add '-t' to an adjective to make an adverb: 'försiktig' becomes 'försiktigt' (carefully) here.
An 'att' clause can act as the subject of the sentence: 'att han kom' (that he came) surprised me.
Use 'den' before 'en' words and 'det' before 'ett' words: 'den nya läraren' (the new teacher), an 'en' word.
You can drop 'som' (that) when it is the object: 'boken jag läser' = the book I am reading.
Use 'i' with compass directions: 'i norr' (in the north), likewise 'i söder', 'i öster', 'i väster'.
The reflexive 'ta för sig' means help yourself to food: 'ta för dig' (help yourself).
The verb 'se ut' (to look) splits and wraps the description: 'ser hotfullt ut' (looks threatening).
'Glad att' plus an infinitive says what you are glad to do: 'glad att träffa dig' (glad to meet you).
After 'jag undrar' (I wonder) the question keeps subject before verb: 'när hon kommer' = when she comes.
'Skjuta upp' is a phrasal verb meaning to postpone: 'jag skjuter upp beslutet' (I postpone the decision).
Make a command negative by putting 'inte' after the verb: 'glöm inte' (don't forget).
